findings.text: Opcode validation accepts only narrow combinations of exit reason with decoded operation and addressing extension. Port and nested fault exits bypass checking, while other exits each require a specific operation encoding, with monitor, wait, timestamp counter read with processor id, debug register seven access and hypercall additionally constraining the addressing extension or register field.

Expected encodings observed are CPUID A20F, cache invalidate 080F, monitor C8 or FA with 010F, wait C9 or FB with 010F, MSR read 320F and write 300F, performance counter 330F, timestamp 310F, timestamp with id F9 with 010F, debug read 210F and write 230F restricted to register seven, hypercall D9 with 010F, writeback invalidate 090F, all hexadecimal.

Port emulation distinguishes string operations from accumulator operations. String operations are bounded by shared buffer capacity divided by element width and by repeat count, use segment base plus index registers with direction flag adjustment, and request reentry while repeat count remains. Scalar operations exchange a width limited accumulator value and require host supplied result validity on reads.

String memory helpers first perform a kernel range probe and then copy element by element in ascending or descending order according to direction. A failed probe yields an exception result with fault metadata, and a failed element access stops the loop and propagates its result.

User mode access to a kernel range address is converted into page fault exception information carrying user indication, optional write indication, faulting address and page fault vector, rather than performing the access.

An address counts as kernel space when at or above the maximum task size, except on 64 bit builds where the legacy system call page is explicitly excluded even though it sits above that threshold. The page test masks the address to page granularity before comparing against the fixed system call page address.

Port exit information layout uses bit 2 for string marker, value 1 for input direction, repeat on bit 3, data width on bits 4 to 6 for byte, word and doubleword, address width on bits 7 to 9 for 16, 32 and 64 bit, segment selector on bits 10 and 11 with zero for extra segment and three for data segment, and port number shifted to bit 16.

Exit information construction maps first opcode byte to operation family and port source. String input and output families record their segment association and take port from DX, immediate families take port from the immediate field, register families take port from DX. Byte opcodes force single byte width, other opcodes select word or doubleword from decoded operand width, address width follows decoded address width, and repeat presence is preserved.
Width limiting keeps only the requested low order bits of a 64 bit value by masking with one less than two raised to the width.

Processor identification handling prefers a protected table lookup and only contacts the host when that lookup reports unsupported. Host exchange publishes input leaves, extended control register state conditioned on operating system save support, and supervisor state for a specific topology leaf when shadow stack is present, then requires validity of all four result registers before committing them to guest state.

The host identification callback context pairs a guest host communication block pointer with an emulation context pointer. Leaf exchange uses function and subfunction inputs and four 32 bit outputs mapped to the corresponding guest registers.
Failure of the host identification callback inside protected lookup handling terminates the guest with a Linux defined CPUID failure reason rather than returning an error to the emulation loop.

Extended control register read takes an index in ECX and combines EDX and EAX into a 64 bit value. Raw model specific register read takes the register number in ECX and splits the 64 bit result into low and high halves.

Timestamp interception while secure timestamp is enabled is treated as host error and guest execution must not trust the supplied counter. Successful host exchange requires validity of timestamp halves, plus auxiliary register validity for the variant that also returns processor id, before updating guest registers.

Emulation context setup clears the whole structure, attaches current registers, and decodes the instruction only for non exception exits defined by an inclusive exit code range. Successful emulation advances guest instruction pointer by decoded length.

Nested exception safety is judged by stack range membership. A trap frame already on the secondary virtualization stack whose previous stack pointer was outside that stack is classified as invalid context and must not proceed to normal handling.

Raw exception handling acquires and releases a per CPU communication block around context setup and exit dispatch. Success advances the instruction, retry does nothing further, forwarded exception injects guest fault state, while unsupported operation, host communication failure and decode failure each report and signal outer failure, and any unknown result is fatal.

Virtualization exception entry splits by privilege after early debug trap handling. Kernel and user paths use different entry and exit wrappers around the shared raw handler, and early boot uses a dedicated static communication block with direct register display and termination on failure rather than the normal per CPU mechanism.

Failure consequences depend on origin. Kernel failure dumps registers then asks the host to terminate and panics if termination returns. User failure delivers a bus error signal with object error code and null address instead of stopping the machine. Invalid nested context panics immediately.

Debug trap recognition compares the exit reason against exception base plus debug vector. Debug traps are handled before entering instrumentable regions to avoid recursion, with separate kernel and user debug helpers.

Trust domain debug reporting prefixes messages with a module tag and maintains indexed name tables for domain attributes and control fields. Dump helpers iterate the tables, print names whose bits are set, clear handled bits, and report any remaining bits as unknown hexadecimal.
Three module call entry symbols provide host initiated calls with increasing preservation semantics: plain call, call with return values, and call with return values plus saved state.
